claims.statement: Allocation exception audit confirms 100% of the 186 held orders fall within scope EXC-0921 (v18 split-reservation, east-node routed), and no held order falls outside that scope.
claims.limitation: The audit itself states this cannot separate an effect of the rule change from an effect specific to the east-node lanes, because only rule-affected orders were routed to the east node at all (perfect confound: cohort and route are identical). It confirms scope, not mechanism.

claims.statement: Working hypothesis: v18's east-first multi-node reservation logic is producing split-reservation exceptions that leave east-node orders allocated but not releasable to carrier pickup.
claims.limitation: Still not discriminating: the exception audit (m8_r_exceptions) confirms the cohort is exactly the rule-v18/east-node set but explicitly cannot separate a rule-side defect from an east-node-side (carrier/dock) effect, since every order in that cohort was also routed to the same node. Handoff-to-carrier evidence is needed to discriminate allocation_rule_defect from carrier_feed_lag/dock_capacity.

next_action.rationale: The exception audit (m8_r_exceptions) confirmed scope but is explicitly confounded and cannot distinguish a rule-side defect from an east-node-side effect. The observability gap (m8_e09/c7) says dashboards don't show how a booked pickup relates to the carrier's own confirmation. Tracing handoffs for scope EXC-0921 directly targets that gap: if allocation never handed these orders off to a carrier pickup booking, that points to allocation_rule_defect; if handoff completed but the carrier never confirmed/collected, that points to carrier_feed_lag or dock_capacity. This is the highest-information read-only diagnostic available and stays within authorized bounds (m8_e07).
